Find a set of unrelated genotyped animals

Source: R/findUnrelated.R
findUnrelated.Rd

Chooses genotyped animals of which no two are related, as many as it can, and gives the same set every time.

Usage

findUnrelated(ped, genotyped)

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam (an unknown parent is NA). Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text; other columns are not read.

genotyped

a logical vector, one value per row of ped: TRUE for an animal that may be chosen (one with DNA, for instance). kinship2's 0/1 avail is given as avail == 1.

Value

A character vector of the chosen ids, in byte order; character(0) when no animal is genotyped.

Details

Two animals are related when they share an ancestor or one descends from the other, which is when their kinship is above 0. The animals are chosen one at a time: among the genotyped animals still in play, the one related to the fewest of them (itself counted) is taken, ties going to the first id in byte order (capitals before lower case), and it and every animal related to it leave play. The counts are taken again after each pick. A swap pass then looks for a chosen animal that can be traded for two left-out animals, each related to it and to no other chosen animal and not related to each other; the first such trade (by chosen animal, then pair, in byte order) is made, any animal now related to no chosen one is added by the same rule, and the pass starts again until no trade is left.

So every two chosen animals are unrelated, no genotyped animal can be added, no chosen animal can be traded for two, and the row order of ped does not change the answer. The set is not always the largest possible one.

Sex is not read, so a male dam or an unknown sex does not matter here, and one known parent is legal. A pedigree from which relatedness cannot be read is refused: findUnrelated() stops, naming the animals, when checkPedigree reports missingIds, duplicateIds, ownParent, cycle, rowlessParents (addParents adds a row for each such parent) or missingParentCodes.

kinship2's pedigree.unrelated() breaks its ties at random, so it can give a different set each time it runs. On the comparison pedigrees its tests use (kinship2's sample.ped families 1 and 2, and a 375-animal rhesus pedigree with 30 percent genotyped), findUnrelated() chooses 4, 2 and 44 animals, the sizes kinship2 1.9.6.2 gave; on the seeded random pedigrees its tests compare, it never chooses fewer animals than kinship2.

See also

checkPedigree, addParents, kinship

Examples

## s1 and d1 are the parents of the full siblings o1 and o2; f1 is
## unrelated to them.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("s1", "d1", "o1", "o2", "f1"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "s1", "s1", NA),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "d1", "d1", NA)
)
## Everyone genotyped: f1, then d1 and s1, who are not related.
findUnrelated(ped, rep(TRUE, 5L))
#> [1] "d1" "f1" "s1"
## Only the offspring and f1 genotyped: one of the siblings and f1.
findUnrelated(ped, ped$id %in% c("o1", "o2", "f1"))
#> [1] "f1" "o1"
